claims.text: Gradient nanostructuring can simultaneously improve material strength and ductility.
Heterostructured nanostructuring can simultaneously improve material strength and ductility.
The proposed processing creates a spatial gradient in grain size or other microstructural features.
The proposed processing can create a composite-like microstructure containing spatially varying phases.
The gradient or heterostructured architecture introduces grain-boundary gradients and phase interfaces.
The imposed gradient or heterostructure promotes strain partitioning.
Harder regions provide strength while softer regions accommodate ductility.
Strain partitioning enhances overall strain hardening.
Enhanced strain hardening delays plastic localization.
Delayed plastic localization helps overcome the strength–ductility trade-off.
Gradient- or heterostructure-processed samples will have higher yield strength than uniformly processed samples.
Gradient- or heterostructure-processed samples will have greater ductility than uniformly processed samples.
Uniformly processed materials with consistent grain structures exhibit a typical inverse relationship between strength and ductility.
The proposed approach is primarily applicable to metals and alloys in which gradient or heterostructured microstructures can feasibly be produced.
Applicability is conditional on other properties, such as corrosion resistance, not being adversely affected.
The quantitative benefits, scalability, and limits in other material classes are uncertain because no eligible direct experimental evidence was provided.
